target_customer: Public and private road owners and road refurbishing contractors, starting in Norway
problem: Road maintenance relies on heavy-oil bitumen and new aggregate, which is costly and carbon heavy. Carbon Crusher grinds the worn road layer and rebinds it with lignin.
business_model: Crushing as a service (CRAAS), project-based service contracts with road owners and refurbishers
product_category: Climate and construction, carbon-negative road repair

founders.name: Haakon Brunell
founders.background_notes: Angel investor in 20+ impact-tech companies per YC page. Education not listed.

founders.name: Hans Arne Flåto
previous_startups: Founded or co-founded more than 20 companies per YC page
founders.background_notes: Industrial experience in defence, energy and electronics; won the Sam Eyde Innovation Prize in 2010 and 2021 per YC page.

founders.name: Kristoffer Roil
previous_startups: Several startups and exits since 2005 per YC page
founders.background_notes: Angel investor in 30+ companies per YC page.

competitors.name: Avantium and Roelofs lignin bio-asphalt
competitors.what: Built a 250 metre test road section on the N987 in Groningen in June 2021 that replaced part of the bitumen in the top layer with lignin, as part of the CHAPLIN XL project.
competitors.traction_then: Pilot test road only, still in testing phase; not marketable yet
competitors.funding_then: EUR 1.5M Dutch government grant to the project in 2020

technical_complexity.rationale: Needs mobile road crushing equipment, a lignin binder formulation that meets road durability specs and field validation, which is standard heavy engineering with some materials science risk.

defensibility.rationale: The binder concept was also being trialled in the Netherlands in 2021 and lignin is a commodity paper-industry byproduct. Little patent or regulatory protection is documented in sources opened.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source opened shows incumbents copying or acquiring the approach by 2026; the company is still listed active.

market_need_then: Road owners faced maintenance backlogs and rising pressure to cut construction emissions; 2022 press (Fast Company, Biofuels Digest, March 2022) covered the carbon-negative claim, which is company-reported and unverified.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain mission-led climate tone in press coverage, claims such as roads removing CO2

branding.community_and_virality: Covered by Fast Company (March 2022), Sifted (May 2024) and several climate outlets, but no evidence of merch or community.

brand_strength.rationale: The name literally describes the service and is memorable, and early press coverage was strong for a Norwegian startup. No evidence of brand-driven growth.

outcome_analysis: Carbon Crusher joined YC in Winter 2022 with an experienced serial-founder team and early positive climate press, and remains listed as active with 21 people. No verified funding round, revenue figure or exit was found, so the story is an unproven early stage company in a slow, capital-heavy road construction market. Whether it succeeded or stalled cannot be judged from public sources.
notes: Company website carboncrusher.io returned HTTP 404 when fetched. Funding figures conflict across aggregators (about 500K USD at Seedtable, 2.11M USD at CB Insights, 15M USD with a Series A at Standout, an EUR 7.4M seed in a CB Insights snippet) and none were confirmed by a press release, so no round is recorded. Education of founders not found. The Sifted feature (May 2024) could not be fetched (403). Competitor list is limited to one dated source; others were not found with date terms. Completeness pass: The one round recorded (pre-seed, about $500K) rests on a single database, Seedtable; date not given there (The Company Check dates a seed to 2022-01-10). Sifted reports an undisclosed amount from Lowercarbon Capital after YC. CB Insights ($2.11M over 4 rounds, Series A 2023-06), Standout ($15M) and Caplight ($15.5M) totals are larger than the recorded round; the gap is unresolved.
